summary: A rewarding short stop on a Talat Noi walk: Holy Rosary, also called Kalawar, combines a pale Gothic Revival façade and stained glass with the history of Bangkok’s Portuguese Catholic community. Treat it as an active parish rather than a guaranteed museum interior; the exterior alone makes a useful neighbourhood landmark.
whyGo: See the distinctive spire and pointed arches of the present church, built in 1891–97.
Look for biblical stained-glass scenes inside if visitor access is available.
Add a different strand of religious history to a walk among Talat Noi’s Chinese shrines, workshops and riverfront lanes.
bestFor: A quiet pause during a Talat Noi walk
Visitors interested in Bangkok’s Catholic and Portuguese connections
skipIf: You need guaranteed interior access at a fixed time.
You would be making a long separate journey solely for a large sightseeing attraction.
duration: Allow 20–40 minutes as a planning estimate; longer only if attending worship or exploring the surrounding neighbourhood.
cost: Free admission is reported by the local visitor guide; transport and any voluntary donation are extra. No official current ticket policy was accessible.
hours: Tourist Bangkok lists daily 08:00–17:30, but current parish visitor hours could not be verified. Other visitor listings differ. Aim for daylight and accept that the church may be closed or reserved for worship.
bestTime: A weekday morning fits a Talat Noi walk and avoids the strongest heat. Visit between services and ask before entering if worship is taking place.
gettingThere: At 1318 Charoen Krung Road, reached through the lanes around Soi Wanit 2/Yotha Road. Marine Department and Si Phraya piers are nearby river approaches; check which boat actually stops there. Hua Lamphong MRT is roughly a 15–20-minute walk, a planning estimate. Use ‘Kalawar Church’ as an alternative destination name.
booking: No sightseeing reservation process was found. Independent visitors normally make a brief stop; verify parish arrangements separately if coming specifically for Mass or Christmas worship.
accessibility: Step-free access, accessible toilets and assistance were not verified. The approach passes school grounds and local lanes; visitors using mobility aids should confirm the usable entrance before a dedicated trip.
practicalTips: Wear modest clothing and keep voices low; this is a working church.
Do not interrupt services or photograph worshippers without consent.
Respect school access controls and avoid photographing pupils while approaching through the grounds.
Combine it with nearby Talat Noi lanes so a closed interior does not derail the outing.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 Christmas service or special visitor-access schedule was confirmed. Christmas observances may change access around 24–25 December; check closer to the day and distinguish attending worship from sightseeing.
uncertainties: Current official opening hours and Mass timetable remain unconfirmed; the parish website returned an access error.
December 2026 events and wheelchair facilities were not verified.
